Key Facts

In ten months, the number of complaints grew by about a third

About 500 complaints were added

Almost 2,600 complaints are coming to eight commissions

Foreigners make up about a quarter of all complaints

Labor Inspectorate legal adviser Olena Smolska said during a live broadcast on Rus.Postimees that artificial intelligence has sharply increased the inspectorate's workload. In ten months, the number of complaints grew by a third, adding about 500 complaints.

Eight labor dispute committees are now facing almost 2,600 complaints. The number of committee members has not changed.

Artificial intelligence makes filing complaints easier, especially for foreigners who do not speak Estonian. They account for about a quarter of all complaints. ## In France, increases without measuring the share of AI

In the documents consulted by ActuIA on their 2025 activity, neither the Council of State, nor the Commission for Access to Administrative Documents (CADA), nor the CNIL (France's data protection authority) quantifies the share of requests written with AI. Volumes are rising. Administrative courts recorded 334,706 cases in 2025, 20% more than in 2024, and their backlog grew by 21.7%, according to the 2025 public report of the Council of State. In its editorial, Didier-Roland Tabuteau, then vice-president of the Council of State, wrote that AI "risks further increasing its workload by facilitating the multiplication of requests". ActuIA has detailed these signals, including two orders from the Grenoble administrative court targeting requests written by AI.

Outside the courts, CADA received 14,721 referrals in 2025, according to Acteurs publics, which consulted its activity report. That is 45% more than the average of the previous four years and more than double 2020. ... According to Acteurs publics, the report does not attribute this increase to AI. The CNIL received 20,150 complaints in 2025, compared with 17,772 in 2024.

Der Landesbeauftragte für den Datenschutz Niedersachsen (LfD), Denis Lehmkemper, hat dem Niedersächsischen Landtag seinen 31. Tätigkeitsbericht vorgelegt. Darin dokumentiert die Aufsichtsbehörde ihre Arbeit im Jahr 2025 und aktuelle Entwicklungen aus dem ersten Halbjahr 2026. Schwerpunkte bilden Künstliche Intelligenz, Cyber-Sicherheit und digitale Souveränität sowie die neuen Transparenzregeln für politische Werbung. Im Jahr 2025 gingen 4.022 Beschwerden beim LfD ein, rund 70 Prozent mehr als im Vorjahr. Auch die Zahl der gemeldeten Datenschutzverletzungen nahm zu. 2025 gingen fünf Prozent mehr als im Vorjahr, im ersten Halbjahr 2026 waren es rund 58 Prozent mehr als im entsprechenden Vorjahreszeitraum. Nach Einschätzung des LfD trägt auch Künstliche Intelligenz zu dieser Entwicklung bei. KI-Chatbots verwiesen bei der Suche nach möglichen Datenschutzverstößen häufig auf Beschwerdemöglichkeiten und erstellten entsprechende Musterschreiben. Erstmals erreichten die Behörde zudem 20 Beschwerden gegen die Betreiber von KI-Systemen.

At the same time, such applications are increasingly found to be legally unfounded, contain inaccuracies, or are based on erroneous arguments.

PTAC notes: AI is capable of quickly preparing convincingly sounding text, however, it is not a legal consultant and does not bear responsibility for the information provided. Often, the user receives confirmation from AI that "the truth is on their side," even though the actual circumstances or legislation say otherwise.

As a result, people submit additional and repeated applications that do not help solve the problem but increase administrative burden.

AI can also refer to inappropriate or already outdated regulations, incorrectly specify procedural deadlines, or prepare legally incorrect claims for an enterprise or court.

Such mistakes can have real consequences - missed deadlines, unfounded demands, and unnecessary financial expenses. PTAC emphasizes: it is impossible to hold AI accountable for incorrect advice; the responsibility for the decision made remains with the user.
